findings.practical_consequence: The terminal six-file handoff cannot be emitted because twelve candidate evidence records violate the exact evidence-index schema, including records supporting the corpus adoption and rollback design. Required correction: Replace every malformed evidence item with the exact seven-field provenance record, using an absolute or package-stable locator, the verified SHA-256, a specific supported fact, and an explicit limitation; then revalidate that every requirement and readiness evidence ID resolves through research_package.py.
evidence: The planner-handoff contract and research_package.py `_indexed_evidence_ids` require every evidence item to contain exactly id, source_kind, source_locator, source_sha256, accessed_at, supported_claim, and limitations.
candidate-round-1.json evidence IDs Y, TSC, TCOR, CW, CA, ICA, SCLD, INST, RMAP, PLC, SRC, and CQ contain only id, path, and sha256.
CUR-002 and FUT-009 requirement statuses cite malformed IDs including Y, TSC, TCOR, CW, and CQ, so these records are not optional unused metadata.

findings.practical_consequence: A planner could incorrectly treat eight external projection targets as already characterized even though the claimed seven-up-to-date/one-missing state is not grounded by evidence available in the frozen envelope. Required correction: Remove the ungrounded current-target-state assertion and make exact existence/hash/parity checks an implementation-time projection preflight, while retaining the grounded target inventory and create-missing behavior. Do not claim target state without an authorized evidence root and per-target evidence record.
evidence: candidate-round-1.json exact_topology.current_target_state asserts `up_to_date_first_seven: true` and `eighth_missing_requires_create_missing: true`.

The envelope authoritative roots include memory-knowledge and mcp-agents-workflow but exclude FCSAPI, taggable-database, taggable-api, united-partners, agentic-trading, and the Documents/Codex target whose file states are included in that assertion.

The cited topology evidence P, A, AL, and CFG establishes generator behavior, the local AGENTS consumer, allowlist membership, and trusted-project configuration; it does not establish current bytes or existence for those external AGENTS.md targets.

findings.practical_consequence: The adoption plan cannot make the required exact corpus rollback tools available to the sync client because the candidate specifies local implementation and tests but omits the deployed-server rollout, verification, and rollback boundary. Required correction: Add a grounded deployment stage before any corpus mutation: cite the authoritative deployment script, name the approval owner and required Azure/commit inputs, verify health/readiness plus exact availability and behavior of both new MCP tools at the deployed endpoint, and define containment or rollback to the prior deployed image. Sequence corpus preflight and writes only after that deployed-tool gate passes.
evidence: candidate-round-1.json exact_corpus_readback_contract states corpus_get_identity and corpus_reconcile_inactive are NOT_IMPLEMENTED and assigns changes to corpus_writer.py, corpus_qdrant.py, workflows/corpus.py, server.py, and sync_corpus.py.

working-agreement/sync_corpus.py targets the deployed endpoint `https://memory-knowledge.azurewebsites.net/mcp/`; local code and unit tests therefore cannot make the new MCP tools callable by the adoption sync.

The candidate adoption and rollback text names canonical edits, projections, managed installation, corpus synchronization, tests, and file/corpus restoration, but names no server deployment prerequisite, deployed tool-availability observable, deployment owner/input, or prior-image rollback.

The accessible authoritative file infra/azure-push.sh provides a concrete Azure build, Web App image update, restart, and health-check route, but it is absent from the evidence index and planner-facing adoption contract.
